fatal_errors: The proposed Co-plus-Hf precipitation treatment does not reconstruct the demonstrated intervention: Re addition to sputtered NbMoTaW films under room-temperature He implantation.
Evidence for Co-induced sigma precipitation comes from Al0.8NbTiV-based alloys and does not establish that 2 at.% Co, aging at 900 °C, or 10–20 nm sigma precipitates will occur in W–Ta–Cr–V–Hf.

The claim that sigma precipitates will preserve irradiation resistance is unsupported; sigma phase can be brittle, and precipitates may instead trap helium, promote interfaces for bubble nucleation, or destabilize under irradiation.
The stated 10–20% strengthening, aging duration, irradiation dose, and service-temperature window are not grounded in the cited evidence.
The baseline is ambiguous between quaternary W–Ta–Cr–V and Hf-containing W–Ta–Cr–V–Hf, preventing clean attribution of any observed effect to Co.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad objective of strengthening an irradiation-tolerant refractory alloy and proposes a reasonably measurable falsification experiment, so its problem alignment and experimental discriminability are fair. However, it is scientifically remote from the hidden result, which concerns Re-induced grain refinement, lattice distortion, excess free volume, and amorphous grain-boundary regions in nanocrystalline NbMoTaW films that suppress grain-boundary helium-bubble accumulation and irradiation embrittlement. The generated mechanism instead relies on sigma-phase precipitation in a different alloy family and under different thermal and irradiation conditions. E1 may support general stability of nanocrystalline W–Ta–Cr–V-related alloys, while E2 supports Co-induced sigma strengthening only in an Al–Nb–Ti–V system. Neither validates transfer to W–Ta–Cr–V–Hf or demonstrates irradiation stability of the proposed precipitates. E3 and E4 provide only broad context and do not support the quantitative predictions. Thus, the idea is novel and testable but presently too speculative to qualify as a well-supported plausible alternative.
